summary: David J. Kalupahana worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He taught at Ceylon (1959–1971) and chaired philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1972.

David John McCutchion specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Jesus College, Cambridge, he taught literature at Visva-Bharati University in 1957, was Reader in Comparative Literature at Jadavpur University (ca. 1960–1972), and visited the University of Sussex (1970–1971).

David Jones works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. By 2007, he was a philosophy professor at the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell. He taught at SOAS University of London (1962–1968), the University of Michigan (1968–1969), and served as history chair at Cornell University (1969–2002).

David Kerman Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, having also studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman. He held an appointment at Smith College.

David Kopf was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Chicago from 1960 to 1964. He subsequently spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving on the faculty from 1967 to 2003.

David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge in 1992, and was attested in a post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington (ca. 1993–2021), where he became Professor Emeritus in 2021.

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, he served at Franklin & Marshall College as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013).

David Llewellyn Snellgrove worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Southampton, Queens' College, and Cambridge under H. W. Bailey and D. R. S. Bailey, he was later a professor at SOAS University of London from 1950 to 1982.

David Lopes specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Curso Superior de Letras and INALCO, subsequently teaching French at the Curso Superior de Letras from 1901 and serving at the University of Lisbon from 1911 to 1937.

David Ludden is a scholar of Indology and history. Educated at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania, he taught at the University of Virginia (1979–1980), the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and became Professor Emeritus at New York University in 2007.

David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan, SIT Graduate Institute, and the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer (Ph.D. 2011), he joined the faculty at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 2011.

David M. Knipe, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Mircea Eliade. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor of South Asian Studies and religious studies chair, later becoming Professor Emeritus.

David Matsumoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004–2013) and as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

David Max Moerman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and Columbia University, where he served as Professor and Department Chair of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures (attested 2026).

David Mitchell specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cleveland State University (2005–2009) and Ohio State University (2009–2019), and he became an Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2015.

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham. He spent his career at El Colegio de México (1970–2010; emeritus 2019), with visiting professorships at Iowa, Harvard, EPHE, and Rome.

David Oliver Allen was an Indologist and historian educated at Amherst College (1819–1823) and Andover Theological Seminary (1824–1827). He served as a missionary with the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions (1827–1853) and led the American Mission Press in 1844.

David Ownby specializes in Chinese history and religious studies. Educated at Vanderbilt and Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University (1989–1993) and served as Professor of History at the Université de Montréal from 1994 to 2023.
